title: Disclosure in Incentivized Reviews: Does It Protect Consumers?
authors: Sungsik Park; Woochoel Shin; Jinhong Xie
eligible_reason: Single event date: post switches on in the same year_month for every product (month 7 in SR.RData, Month_nr.RData, Month_nr_c.RData and SR_c.RData; checked with R), consistent with Amazon's platform-wide incentivized-review policy change. Tables 4-6 are treatment:post DiDs with product (or product-platform) FE and year_month FE; Table 5 col 1 has no controls but has one adoption cohort. Tables 2-3 and 7 are review-level regressions on disclosure/Vine indicators.
design_notes: R/fixest. Table 4: feols(log(sales) ~ log(nr_e_IR) + ar_e_IR + log(price) + log(age):category + treatment:post | p_id + year_month), groups by delta-r. Table 5: feols(log1p(n_r1) ~ treatment:post | p_id + year_month) and cross-platform version (p_id_site). Table 6: cross-platform sales with controls. Month_nr: 4,078 products x 11 months, post = months 7-11 for all.
n_adoption_cohorts_note: post = 1 from year_month 7 for all units; the apparent extra first-post months in SR.RData come from products entering the unbalanced panel after month 7.
data_provenance_note: Collected Amazon (and cross-platform) review and sales-rank data with anonymized product ids; no statement of synthetic data.
screener_notes: Screened from package only. Not staggered: common post date verified from shipped data.
